l4_steps.name: Activate Winter Operations Plan via AMS
l4_steps.input: Meteorological forecast showing OAT <= +3°C or freezing precipitation expected within 2 hours
l4_steps.output: WINOPS activation notice distributed to ground crews, ramp supervisors, and flight dispatch
l4_steps.kpi: Activation lead time >= 2 hours before first affected departure; 100% crew acknowledgement within 15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Late NOTAMs or rapidly developing weather compress the activation window; insufficient crew briefing time during sudden temperature drops leads to unprepared ground teams

l4_steps.name: Pre-Position De-icing Equipment and Brief Crews
l4_steps.input: WINOPS activation notice, flight schedule, de-icing pad/gate assignments
l4_steps.output: De-icing vehicles positioned at pad or gates; crews briefed, signed off on fluid handling procedures
l4_steps.kpi: Equipment readiness >= 30 min before first scheduled de-icing event; all crew holdover time (HOT) training current within 12 months
l4_steps.pain_point: GSE unserviceability during peak winter events reduces available truck count with no redundancy at smaller stations; crew HOT training currency lapses go undetected until seasonal activation

l4_steps.name: Confirm Fluid Inventory and Type Availability
l4_steps.input: Current fluid stock levels (Type I, II, III, IV), upcoming flight schedule, forecast storm duration
l4_steps.output: Fluid availability confirmed and logged; reorder triggered if stock < 40% of estimated daily requirement
l4_steps.kpi: Fluid stock >= 120% of estimated daily requirement; reorder threshold: 40% remaining; no event aborted due to fluid shortage
l4_steps.pain_point: Type IV fluid supply chain disruptions during extended winter events common at capacity-constrained stations; airports with limited glycol storage cannot buffer multi-day storm events

l4_steps.name: Monitor Real-Time Weather and Issue De-icing Advisory
l4_steps.input: METAR, TAF, PIREP, real-time OAT, precipitation type and rate from DTN feeds
l4_steps.output: De-icing advisory issued specifying contamination type, severity level, and recommended fluid type
l4_steps.kpi: Advisory issued within 10 min of METAR update confirming frozen precipitation; advisory accuracy vs actual ramp conditions >= 90%
l4_steps.pain_point: Rapidly changing precipitation type (freezing rain transitioning to snow) invalidates HOT mid-event; DTN update latency vs real-time ramp microclimate conditions can lead to under- or over-treatment decisions

l4_steps.name: Conduct Aircraft Contamination Walk-Around Inspection
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) — Mobile Ops Tablet
l4_steps.input: Aircraft parked at gate or de-icing pad, current weather conditions, contamination advisory
l4_steps.output: Contamination type and surface coverage documented (wings, fuselage, tail, control surfaces, sensors)
l4_steps.kpi: Inspection completed within 5 min of aircraft block-in; 100% of critical surfaces (wing leading edge, ailerons, elevator, rudder, pitot tubes) checked
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew access to tail surfaces restricted at narrow-body gates without elevated stands; time pressure from tight turnarounds causes rushed inspections that miss contamination on aft fuselage or horizontal stabiliser

l4_steps.name: Determine De-Icing Treatment Type and Fluid Selection
l4_steps.input: Contamination type (frost, snow, ice, freezing rain), OAT, precipitation rate, planned departure time
l4_steps.output: Treatment order specifying: Type I only vs. Type I + anti-icing fluid, dilution ratio, and sequence
l4_steps.kpi: Treatment type decision within 3 min of inspection completion; fluid selection compliant with SAE AMS 1424 (Type I) and AMS 1428 (Type IV) specifications
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew chiefs without current SAE HOT table training select incorrect dilution ratios, overestimating holdover time and creating latent safety risk; audit trail for treatment decision not captured in all DMS implementations

l4_steps.name: Position De-icing Vehicle and Establish Cockpit Communication
l4_steps.input: Treatment order, aircraft stand or pad assignment, vehicle positioning clearance from ramp controller
l4_steps.output: Vehicle positioned within safe working envelope; two-way communication established with flight deck; chocks and safety cones confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Spray basket clearance >= 1 m from aircraft surface at all times; positioning complete within 3 min of vehicle arrival at stand
l4_steps.pain_point: Ramp congestion at hub airports delays vehicle access to stand; ATC-mandated de-icing pad queuing adds 15–20 min to turnaround during peak demand; inadequate ground lighting at night complicates safe vehicle positioning

l4_steps.name: Apply Type I Heated Fluid — Active Contamination Removal
l4_steps.input: Contaminated aircraft surfaces, Type I fluid heated to 60–82°C, application nozzle settings
l4_steps.output: Aircraft surfaces cleared of snow, ice, and frost; fluid volume applied and temperature at nozzle logged in DMS
l4_steps.kpi: All critical surfaces clear of contamination after Type I pass; fluid temperature >= 60°C at application point; fluid waste rate < 5% through overspray
l4_steps.pain_point: Very low OAT (<-15°C) reduces Type I heated fluid effectiveness, requiring multiple passes and extending turnaround; excessive Type I application increases glycol runoff requiring EPA/Transport Canada environmental reporting

l4_steps.name: Apply Anti-Icing Fluid (Type II/IV) for Holdover Protection
l4_steps.input: Clean aircraft surfaces confirmed, selected anti-icing fluid and dilution ratio, OAT, precipitation rate
l4_steps.output: Anti-icing fluid coat applied uniformly; application start time, volume, dilution ratio, and fluid type recorded to DMS with timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Application completed within 3 min; fluid start time logged to second-level accuracy for HOT calculation; coating uniform per SAE AMS 1428 visual check
l4_steps.pain_point: Type IV fluid viscosity at OAT < -14°C reduces flow-off performance on wing surfaces, requiring switch to Type III or abandoning anti-icing and increasing re-treatment frequency; operators must carry multiple fluid types adding storage and logistics complexity

l4_steps.name: Calculate Holdover Time from FAA/TC Tables via EFB
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen FliteDeck (EFB — FAA/TC HOT Table Application)
l4_steps.input: Anti-icing fluid type, dilution ratio, application start time, OAT, precipitation type and rate
l4_steps.output: HOT start and end times calculated and communicated to flight crew via ACARS or verbal relay
l4_steps.kpi: HOT calculation completed within 2 min of anti-icing fluid application start; communicated to captain before pushback clearance request; zero cases of HOT communicated after pushback initiation
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA/TC HOT tables are conservative estimates; actual holdover time reduced by wind, direct sunlight, taxiway delays — flight crews must perform independent pre-departure contamination check but training and procedures vary by airline; EFB app connectivity failures force manual table lookup

l4_steps.name: Conduct Post-Application Clean Aircraft Inspection
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) — Mobile Ops Tablet
l4_steps.input: Anti-icing fluid applied, aircraft surfaces, current precipitation conditions
l4_steps.output: Clean aircraft confirmation issued or re-treatment ordered; inspection result logged with crew ID and timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Inspection covers 100% of critical surfaces; completion within 5 min of fluid application finish; re-treatment rate < 8% of treated aircraft
l4_steps.pain_point: Inadequate ramp lighting during night ops or heavy snowfall reduces visibility for post-application inspectors; incorrect clean aircraft calls are a primary de-icing safety risk (referenced in multiple NTSB and TSB accident reports); no standardised photographic evidence requirement at most carriers

l4_steps.name: Issue De-Icing Completion Record and Transmit to Flight Crew
l4_steps.input: DMS treatment record (fluid type, volume, dilution, start/end time, HOT range), clean aircraft confirmation
l4_steps.output: De-icing completion report transmitted to flight deck via ACARS; paper copy retained for regulatory compliance per FAA AC 120-60B
l4_steps.kpi: Report transmitted >= 5 min before pushback; 100% compliance with FAA pre-takeoff contamination check communication requirement; zero ACARS transmission failures without verbal backup
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS data entry errors under time pressure cause incorrect HOT communication to crew; regional and charter operations rely on verbal communication with no digital audit trail, creating regulatory exposure; captains not trained to question HOT plausibility against observed conditions

l4_steps.name: Coordinate Pushback Within HOT Window
l4_steps.input: HOT end time, ATC ground departure sequence, aircraft readiness confirmation, tug availability
l4_steps.output: Pushback clearance issued within HOT validity window; ATC ground movement coordination confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Departure initiated >= 5 min before HOT expiry; on-time departure rate (D0) >= 78% during active winter ops; zero aircraft departing with documented expired HOT
l4_steps.pain_point: ATC sequencing delays during high-demand winter events push departures beyond HOT expiry, requiring return to pad for costly re-treatment; airlines report 18–25 min average re-treatment penalty per aircraft during peak de-icing, cascading across the departure bank

l4_steps.name: Monitor Departure Queue for HOT Expiry and Re-Treatment Triggers
l4_steps.input: Real-time departure queue timestamps, HOT end times per aircraft, updated weather data from DTN
l4_steps.output: Re-treatment orders issued for aircraft exceeding HOT; ATC notified of delay and sequence changes
l4_steps.kpi: Re-treatment decision made >= 10 min before HOT expiry; zero aircraft cleared for takeoff with expired HOT; re-treatment throughput capacity >= scheduled de-icing volume + 20% buffer
l4_steps.pain_point: Simultaneous HOT expiry across multiple aircraft during heavy snowfall creates ramp congestion and cascading departure delays; single de-icing pad airports cannot handle re-treatment surges without significant schedule disruption; AMS does not natively flag HOT expiry without custom integration

l4_steps.name: Log De-Icing Event Data for Compliance and Performance Analysis
l4_steps.input: DMS treatment records (fluid volumes, times, tail numbers, crew IDs), HOT data, weather data, delay records
l4_steps.output: De-icing event records archived; fluid consumption and waste report generated; seasonal performance dashboard updated
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of de-icing events logged within 24 hours; fluid waste rate < 5% of applied volume; regulatory audit trail completeness >= 99.5%; glycol runoff report submitted to EPA/Transport Canada within 30 days of season-end
l4_steps.pain_point: DMS data silos prevent automated correlation with on-time performance and maintenance data, limiting root-cause analysis; EPA and Transport Canada glycol runoff reporting requirements vary by airport and add manual compliance burden; data quality issues in DMS (manual entries, missing fields) degrade seasonal analytics
